There is not one country in the world that considers Sealand a real sovereign country. If you declared yourself beholden to the laws of Sealand no one would take you seriously.

Forgetting all of the extremely difficult practical issues, including finding anyone willing to contract with your government, I would take a strong guess that its because Sealand's claim to sovereignty is extremely weak.

So Sealand is 12 miles off the coast of Britain. Originally there was some question on this and a 1960's court opinion suggested Sealand may have independent legal status. In 1987, the UK extended its territorial waters to 12 miles. Moreover the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) set the same limit. Which the UK and the Eurozone have agreed to. In UK territorial waters, UK law applies. This obviously includes the law of copyright and the various speech limitations found under UK law.

There's also an issue about artificial versus natural islands in the convention but its pretty much splitting hairs. It is an interesting issue though.

1. Infrastructure; Sealand is not really an option, They were going to offer hosting, but closed down in 2008. The problem whoever is hosting has to connect to the internet somehow, and they have to abide by some rules in order to do that. The darknet sideswipes the issue, but then there's no main stream exposure. Panama seems to be the most lenient along with a few others, and that's where VOAT is now.

  2. No matter where you host, if you piss off enough people, you can have problems. Look at North Korea. They get their internet from China, and therefore are limited in what they can get and feed to the internet. If China shuts them off, they have nothing. That can happen to other places too if there is enough political pressure.

  3. Just because you claim to be a resident of Sealand will not stop another country from arresting you. Even if you "incorporate" in Sealand, this doesn't protect you from the laws of another country if they believe you have violated them. Look at Snowden and what he had to go through, and is still going through. Do you think he can just take a vacation to the Bahamas?

  4. Countries can always block your shit. China does it, Japan does it, Saudi Arabia does it, In fact, a whole shitload censor the web in one way or another.

Basically, sovereignity is based on either:

Factual recognition (some sovereign organization is making official treaties with them)

Actual recognition (% of sovereign states vote for recognizing the state)

Then there is that tiny detail, that in order to allow legal protection of foreigners (including foreign capital and corporations), there have to be official treaties solving the matters between two sovereign entities (not only states are considered as sovereigns on the fields of international law).

Basically, nothing is stopping you from doing so, problem is, anytime you would try to operate your corporation outside of borders of your recognized/unrecognized Sealand (Sealand recognition is somewhat complicated), you would be doing so most likely illegaly and you would be subjected to sanctions from affected countries.

It's an interesting idea to explore, but it really depends on what sort of limit you're talking about. I have a lot of interests, and even just a single interest could encompass ten subverses. An example would be, I like comic books so I'd sub to /v/comicbooks, but I'm also a fan of Marvel, and I'm trying to get into DC so I'd sub to those subverses too for a more concentrated news output. But going deeper I'm a fan of Deadpool, Static, Green Arrow, Moon Knight, Ant-Man, Daredevil, and a slew of other comics that potentially have their own dedicated subverses. Just with that example it's 9.

Overall, I think it would be something that would be hard to implement without driving the userbase away. Arbitrarily restricting access to information/content/discussion/etc. and forcing a user to settle with x things is a great way to alienate users, and push them away from a site. When you get down to the base of it, Voat is a discussion board. Restricting it's main purpose discussion won't promote growth, and if it's not allowed to grow then it's very easy for things to become an echo chamber.
